# Custer County Courthouse (South Dakota)

The Custer County Courthouse is a historic government building located in Custer, South Dakota, serving as the seat of government for Custer County.

## Location and Basic Information
- **Address**: 420 Mt. Rushmore Road, Custer, South Dakota
- **County Seat**: Custer is the county seat of Custer County, located in the Black Hills region of southwestern South Dakota

## Historical Significance
The courthouse is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. It was added to the register in 1977.

## Architecture and Construction
The building was constructed in 1881, making it one of the older courthouses in South Dakota. It is a notable example of late 19th-century public architecture in the region. The original structure has been preserved as a historic site, while county government functions may use additional or newer facilities.

## Current Use
The historic courthouse building functions today primarily as a museum—the **1881 Courthouse Museum**—operated by the Custer County Historical Society. The museum features exhibits on local history, including:
- Native American (Lakota) artifacts and history
- Mining and pioneer history of the Black Hills
- The Custer Expedition of 1874, which discovered gold in the area
- Local frontier history

## Historical Context
Custer County was established during the Black Hills Gold Rush era, with the town of Custer being founded in 1875 after gold was discovered by the George Armstrong Custer-led expedition. The courthouse reflects the rapid development of the area following the gold rush.
